paragraphs.text: A **cash-secured put** is a short put position in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned [S1]. The writer sells the put, collects the premium up front, and accepts the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract at the strike any time before expiration [S1]. In a margin account the broker holds only a **margin requirement**, a fraction of the purchase price computed under exchange and FINRA minimum rules, and the writer keeps the rest of their buying power free for other positions [S6]. **LEAPS** (Long-term Equity AnticiPation Securities) is the exchanges' name for listed options with more than a year until expiration [S3].

Every option premium can be split into two parts. **Intrinsic value** is the amount by which the option is in the money: for a call, the stock price minus the strike when positive, otherwise zero; for a put, the strike minus the stock price when positive, otherwise zero [S4]. **Extrinsic value**, also called time value, is everything else: premium minus intrinsic value [S4]. A **poor man's covered call** is a two-leg position: a long, deep in-the-money LEAPS call (expiring a year or more out) and a short, near-term, out-of-the-money call on the same stock [S5].

The allocation split the strategy budget into {{allocation.csp_pct|pct}} for cash-secured puts, {{allocation.leaps_pct|pct}} for LEAPS, and {{allocation.cash_pct|pct}} held as cash, in a **{{regime.label}}** regime with the VIX at {{regime.vix}} and a risk-free rate of {{regime.risk_free_rate_pct|pct}}. The universe covered {{counts.underlyings_screened}} underlyings.

**Assignment** is the process by which an option writer is selected to fulfil the obligation of a contract that a holder has exercised [S2]. When a put holder exercises, some put writer is obliged to take the shares at the strike [S2]. The OCC assigns exercise notices at random to clearing members with short positions in the same series, and each clearing member then assigns its own customers by a method approved by the exchanges [S2].
